summary: Bruno Snell (1896–1986) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Edinburgh (~1919–1920), Oxford (~1921–1922), and Göttingen (~1920–1924), and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~1925–1964).

Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and under Jacqueline I. Stone and others, later serving as assistant professor of religious studies at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017–2019).

Bryan J. Cuevas works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying under Donald Phillip Verene at Emory (1987) and Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano at Virginia (PhD attested 2000), he was a Princeton postdoctoral fellow and professor at Florida State (attested 2008–2021).
Bryan W. Van Norden (born 1962) specializes in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Stanford University and held the James Monroe Taylor Chair in Philosophy at Vassar College (~1996–2023).

Bryce Ryan (1911–2005) worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Washington (BA 1928–1932) and Harvard (MA 1936–1937, PhD 1937–1940), later teaching at Iowa State, Rutgers, Ceylon, Cornell, Wayne State, and Miami.

Buddhadeb Gorai specializes in philosophy and Indology. He earned an MA from Jadavpur University (2006–2008), served as assistant professor at Deshbandhu College for Girls (2014), and founded the Bhāratāyana IKS Journal as editor-in-chief (2026).

Buddhike Indrasena specializes in Indology and medicine. He completed degrees at Peradeniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Medicine, the Postgraduate Institute of Agriculture, and RCS Edinburgh and England, serving in various hospital surgical posts from 2000 through 2020.

Buddhodev Ghosh works in Indology and philosophy. He held a project-teaching assistance post at IIT Bombay (2022) and served as a project associate at the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (2024–2025).

Bulcsu Siklós specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden, and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

Bunga Fukui (1934–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the EPHE under Paul Demiéville, Max Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda (~1978–2004).

Bunkyo Aoki (1886–1956) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University, was a disciple of Kozui Otani (~1910–1914), and taught Tibetan at the University of Tokyo in 1951.

Bunsaku Kurata (1918–1983) worked in Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda, held positions with the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, and was director of Nara National Museum in 1975.

Bunyiu Nanjio (1849–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied at Otani University and Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller, later holding leadership and teaching posts at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and Nagoya Futsū Gakkō.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto (1869–1944) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Karl Florenz at the University of Tokyo and later served as professor and president of Kyoto University.

Burchard Brentjes (1929–2012) worked in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Heinz Mode at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1947–1952), where he also held an academic post (~1954–1971).

Burkard Wilhelm Leist (1819–1906) was a legal historian and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen, Heidelberg, and Berlin under Friedrich Carl von Savigny, later serving as professor of law at Basel (1846), Rostock (1847), and Jena (1853).
Burkhard Quessel is a scholar of Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was attested as a member in 1997, and worked as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

Burmansah Burmansah is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Universitas Komputer Indonesia (2004–2008) and the State University of Jakarta (2014–2016), and was appointed lecturer at STIAB Jinarakkhita in 2020.

Burton Stein (1926–1996) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Illinois Chicago and the University of Chicago (MA ~1950–1954), later holding posts at the University of Hawaiʻi (1965–1983) and SOAS (1983).

Burton Watson (1925–2017) was a sinologist and Japanologist. He studied at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University, later holding faculty posts at Columbia (1961) and Stanford (~1964–1965).
